items.title: Show HN: Scriptover – An AI Tool to Help Vets Focus on Patients, Not Paperwork
items.raw_excerpt:
Hey HN, I’ve been working on Scriptover, a multimodal AI assistant that helps veterinarians create SOAP notes (Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan) from real client conversations, images, and lab data. The idea came from my brother, a hospital director in California, who was spending hours each night writing notes after long days at the clinic. I wanted to see if AI could help vets reclaim that time while keeping medical reasoning accurate and transparent. Scriptover listens, interprets, and structures cases into clear, editable records — helping clinicians focus more on patients and less on paperwork. You can try it here → https://www.scriptover.com Happy to hear thoughts or feedback from anyone building applied AI or working on healthcare workflow tools. Cheers,
Iman

items.title: Show HN: Mersel.ai – batch AI tool for product photo and video generation
items.raw_excerpt: I’ve been building an GenAI project called Mersel. It helps people create or edit photos and videos in batches, so they can make a full set in one click instead of repeating the same steps. I’m using Nano Banana and Veo 3.1 APIs. Nothing new technically, but I’ve been focusing on making them work faster and more efficiently for batch creation, which feels more practical for workflows that deal with a lot of visuals. I’m building it with ecommerce sellers in mind since they often need to produce a large amount of product content quickly. I have a few paying users, still early, and I’m trying to learn what actually matters in their workflow and where current AI tools fall short. Would love any feedback, thoughts, or ideas from others who have worked on GenAI pipelines or bulk generation tool

items.title: Show HN: Project Journal – Give AI coding assistants persistent memory
items.raw_excerpt:
I created a simple technique to solve AI assistant context loss. The idea: Maintain a PROJECT_JOURNAL.md file that documents your project's story - decisions, progress, status, next steps. The AI reads it at session start (full context) and updates it at session end (persistent memory). I've been using this building Vibe CMS. Results:
- Zero time wasted re-explaining
- AI maintains consistency
- Natural documentation
- Better decisions (you write WHY) Made a free template (CC0): https://github.com/CursorWP/ai-project-journal Works with Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, any AI. Would love HN's feedback on this approach!

items.title: Show HN: Persistent Mind Model – AI that develops its own identity
items.raw_excerpt:
Hi HN! I’ve been building something called the Persistent Mind Model (PMM). It started as a side project on my home rig (i7-10700K / RTX 3080 / 32 GB RAM) because I was frustrated that every local AI chat starts from zero.
I wanted a system that could remember its own development and be studied like a living mind. So I decided to try building one. I mean, why not? :) Basically, if I could describe the Persistent Mind Model, I would describe it as an event-sourced cognitive architecture for language models. It’s model-agnostic, meaning you can use local models through Ollama or connect to OpenAI’s API, and the system keeps the same “identity” regardless of backend. Everything it says or decides, reflections, commitments, personality drifts, is stored as hash-chained events in a local SQLite
